name: Camaro Dragon
iocPatterns: Malicious ZIP attachment used in spear‑phishing campaigns
ISO image delivery as attack vector
Legitimate module names embedding backdoor code (e.g., SALTWATER, SEASIDE)
Self‑signed SSL certificates masquerading C2 traffic
Malicious vSphere Installation Bundle used to install hypervisor backdoors
keyCapabilities: Distributes TinyNote backdoor for remote access
Utilizes custom router implants to compromise network infrastructure
Shares malware like Poison Ivy and PlugX across campaigns
Develops cross‑platform malware in Python, Golang and Rust
Uses spear‑phishing via Discord, Google Drive, Slack and Telegram with malicious ZIP archives or links
Employs ISO images as a delivery vector
Creates an all‑in‑one espionage tool that discovers and exfiltrates files, captures screenshots, uploads/downloads files and executes commands
Distributes compiled Python downloader scripts in ELF binaries
Exploits Windows Print Spooler vulnerability (CVE‑2022‑38028) for privilege escalation and credential theft via GooseEgg
Zero‑day exploits Barracuda Email Security Gateway (CVE‑2023‑2868) using TAR file attachments to run arbitrary commands and exfiltrate data
Installs backdoors VIRTUALPITA and VIRTUALPIE on ESXi hypervisors through malicious vSphere Installation Bundles
Masquerades malware with legitimate module names and self‑signed certificates to evade detection
recommendedActions: Patch and harden the Windows Print Spooler service to mitigate CVE‑2022‑38028.
Deploy defenses against exploitation of Barracuda ESG CVE‑2023‑2868, including application layer filtering for TAR attachments.
Monitor outbound traffic for unexpected ISO images, ZIP archives or TAR files delivered via Discord/Drive/Slack/Telegram.
Implement robust email filtering and quarantine policies to detect crafted spear‑phishing messages with LNK or archive attachments.
Enable EDR monitoring for file discovery/exfiltration tools, screenshot utilities, and remote execution commands.
Isolate ESXi hypervisors from management networks; enforce strict authentication and review vSphere Installation Bundles before installation.
Validate SSL/TLS certificates of outgoing traffic; flag self‑signed or untrusted certificates.
campaignsText: Camaro Dragon’s campaign footprint centers on repeated exploitation of high‑impact vulnerabilities and the reuse of known backdoors across multiple regions. Since early 2023, it has been linked to a European healthcare institution that deployed a TinyNote backdoor discovered by Check Point researchers. The actor’s activity is observed as frequent: new phishing vectors (ZIP, TAR, ISO) appear regularly, while a core suite of persistence tools remains constant. The group demonstrates a clear pattern of leveraging the same infrastructure for spear‑phishing, lateral movement and exfiltration, indicating a mature operational cycle. Notably, cross‑platform toolkits were seen in both IT education and defense contexts, underscoring their broad reach.
description: Camaro Dragon is a China-linked advanced persistent threat that focuses on espionage against government, defense and critical infrastructure organizations worldwide. The group commonly uses spear‑phishing with malicious .lnk attachments and distributes the TinyNote backdoor, while re‑using popular malware such as Poison Ivy and PlugX across campaigns. Recent activity in 2023 has highlighted cross‑platform toolkits, zero‑day exploitation of Windows Print Spooler (CVE‑2022‑38028) and Barracuda ESG (CVE‑2023‑2868), and a consistent pattern of exfiltration over covert C2 channels.
goals: Camaro Dragon’s overarching objective is strategic espionage, seeking privileged access to sensitive information from government agencies, defense contractors, critical infrastructure operators, NGOs and think‑tanks. By leveraging widely used communication platforms for phishing delivery and deploying a versatile backdoor, the actor can infiltrate diverse environments across multiple geographies, including China, US, EU, India and ASEAN nations. The group targets entities that hold policy, technological or strategic value, enabling it to harvest intelligence that supports broader geopolitical objectives.
